The first public test of **termfps**: a first-person shooter that runs entirely in your terminal. No GPU, one small file, no install.

This is a **test release**: please play it and tell me what you think with the [feedback form](https://github.com/BunnyPraneeth5/termfps/issues/new?template=feedback.yml). Is the ammo too low? Is an enemy unfair? Does it run well in your terminal?

## Download

| System | File |
|---|---|
| Windows 10/11 (64-bit) | `termfps-v0.75-windows-amd64.zip` |
| Linux (64-bit Intel/AMD) | `termfps-v0.75-linux-amd64.tar.gz` |
| Linux (64-bit ARM, e.g. Raspberry Pi 4/5) | `termfps-v0.75-linux-arm64.tar.gz` |

**Windows first.** The game is made and played on Windows Terminal. The Linux builds pass the same automated tests but haven't been played much yet. There's no macOS build for now (it can't be tested yet).

### Windows: "Windows protected your PC"

The game isn't signed (signing costs money), so Windows may warn you:
- **SmartScreen** ("Windows protected your PC"): click **More info**, then **Run anyway**.
- **Smart App Control** may block it outright ("An Application Control policy has blocked this file"). Restarting Windows has cleared it in testing. Turning Smart App Control off fixes it for good, but Windows can't turn it back on without a reinstall, so only do that if you understand the trade-off. You can also build the game yourself from the source (see the README).

Unzip it, open **Windows Terminal**, go to the folder and run `.\termfps.exe`.

### Linux

```sh
tar xzf termfps-v0.75-linux-amd64.tar.gz
cd termfps-v0.75-linux-amd64
./termfps
```

Use a truecolor terminal (kitty, WezTerm, GNOME Terminal, Konsole...). Sound needs PulseAudio or PipeWire; without it the game runs silently and says why.

## What's in it

- Six maps that unlock as you survive: The Arena, The Warehouse, The Yard, The Tunnel, The Office, The Subway.
- Five enemies (zombie, shooter, runner, tank, exploder) that learn as the tiers go up: they hear your gunshots, shooters hide, zombies surround you, and camping starts a hunt.
- Three guns (pistol, shotgun, rifle), medkits, armor, red barrels and acid.
- Endless **survival** and a 10-wave **waves** mode, with bests saved for every map.
- Stereo sound that comes from where things happen; all sounds generated by the game.
- An in-game guide with 3D views of every enemy, gun and pickup.
- Four looks: half-block pixels, shade blocks, ASCII and mixed (`V` switches).

Needs a terminal of at least 80x24 characters. `termfps -version` prints the version.

**SHA256SUMS.txt** has the checksums of the files.

termfps is open source under the [MIT License](https://github.com/BunnyPraneeth5/termfps/blob/main/LICENSE). Each download includes the licenses of the libraries it's built with (THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt).
